commands.verify_fast: npm run lint && npm run format:check
commands.verify_full: npm run lint && npm run format:check && npm run build
commands.$comment: test:rules needs the Firestore emulator and a JDK on PATH. It is not in verify_full because it is slow and only matters when firebase/firestore.rules changed — run it there and before the release pull request. Say plainly if the JDK is missing and it could not run; never report it as passing.

commit.$comment: Conventional Commits adopted 2026-08-19. Earlier history is free-form imperative and is never rewritten, so the log is mixed by design.

ci.$comment: ci.yml triggers on pull_request into master and release/**, and it is present on release/0.3.0 but NOT yet on master. GitHub takes the workflow from the pull request's BASE branch, so pull requests into release/0.3.0 are checked while the release pull request into master is not. Run verify_full locally before that one and say so in its body. Flip checks_prs_into_base to true once a release merge has carried ci.yml onto master.

release.$comment: Private app: a release is a tag plus a GitHub release, nothing more. Unlike kreobuddha-ui this workflow has NO branch guard of its own — dispatching it against another ref would tag that ref. Always pass --ref master.

post_tag: gh release view v{version} — notes match the CHANGELOG section
confirm the Deploy workflow run for the release merge commit on master succeeded
open the live demo and smoke-test create session / vote / reveal
if firebase/firestore.rules changed, confirm the rules deploy step in that run succeeded

deploy.$comment: Merging the release pull request into master IS the production deploy. That is an extra reason the merge is Rustam's action and never Claude's.
